newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnair downplays possible fuel truckers' strike.
newsitem.headline: Finnair downplays possible fuel truckers' strike.

text.p: Finnish national carrier Finnair Oy said on Friday that a possible strike affecting aircraft fuelling operations would not ground international flights and that as many domestic flights as possible would also fly.

"All international flights would be handled, and as many domestic flights as possible," Finnair spokesman Usko Maatta told Reuters, but he added that the precise impact of the threatened action on Finnair operations was still unknown.

The Finnish transport workers union AKT on Thursday threatened that aircraft fuel truckers at the Helsinki-Vantaa international airport may go on strike next week to support striking airport bus drivers who demand a collective contract.
"If fuelling at Helsinki-Vantaa airport is halted, the planes will be tanked elsewhere," Maatta said. "There are airports outside of Finland, too."
The bus drivers' strike is due to begin on Monday at 0400 GMT if no deal is reached in talks on Sunday, but no precise date has been given for the planned support strike.
Finnair has no direct part in the labour dispute, which is between air terminal bus drivers and airport services company Suomen Lentoasemapalvelut Oy, owned by the Finnish aviation authority.
An AKT union spokesman told Reuters the fuel truckers had no demands of their own.
